Disease relationship: SLE, Sjögren, MS, type 1 diabetes and B-cell-driven autoimmunity; central T-B/APC costimulation node.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Dapirolizumab pegol phase 3 SLE; dazodalibep phase 3 Sjögren; frexalimab phase 2/3 MS/SLE/T1D.
Antibody MoA: Fc-silent or non-crosslinking blockade of CD40L-CD40.
Safety concerns: Thrombosis/platelet activation, infection, broad immune suppression.
Differentiation hypothesis: Safer valency/Fc engineering and biomarker-selected costimulation-high disease can revisit historically strong biology.

Location class: Membrane receptor on mature B cells
Disease relationship: Sjögren, SLE, SSc, autoimmune cytopenias; survival of autoreactive B cells.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Ianalumab/VAY736 phase 3 Sjögren/SLE; no broad approved BAFF-R mAb confirmed.
Antibody MoA: Blocking BAFF binding with Fc-silent modulation or calibrated depletion.
Safety concerns: Infection, hypogammaglobulinemia, vaccine response impairment.
Differentiation hypothesis: More receptor-selective B-cell control than BAFF ligand blockade; Fc tuning can separate blockade from depletion.

Disease relationship: Pathogenic IgG diseases: pemphigus/BP, myositis, AAV, SLE/Sjögren subsets, gMG/CIDP.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab, nipocalimab approved/advanced in IgG-mediated diseases.
Antibody MoA: Block IgG recycling to lower autoantibodies.
Safety concerns: Infections, hypo-IgG, rebound, albumin effects depending molecule.
Differentiation hypothesis: Crowded target; differentiation must be disease-specific dosing, albumin sparing, deeper/controlled IgG lowering or combination design.

Disease relationship: IgG4-RD, SLE, Sjögren, NMOSD, autoimmune cytopenias; broader B lineage than CD20.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Inebilizumab approved in NMOSD and reported approved IgG4-RD/gMG; obexelimab is CD19xFcGR2B in phase 2/3.
Antibody MoA: Depletion or inhibitory co-ligation.
Safety concerns: Infection, hypogammaglobulinemia, prolonged depletion.
Differentiation hypothesis: Non-depleting CD19xFcGR2B can suppress B cells while avoiding full cytotoxic depletion.

Location class: Membrane inhibitory Fc receptor on B cells/myeloid cells
Disease relationship: Immune-complex and B-cell tolerance checkpoint; relevant to SLE, IgG4-RD, pemphigus, autoimmune cytopenias.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Obexelimab targets CD19 and FCGR2B.
Antibody MoA: Bispecific co-ligation with BCR/CD19 to inhibit activation.
Safety concerns: Unwanted immune-complex effects, thrombocytopenia/myeloid modulation, underdosing.
Differentiation hypothesis: Antibody-specific inhibitory bispecific biology; avoids cell depletion.

Disease relationship: Ectopic lymphoid structures and B-cell follicle recruitment in Sjögren, SLE nephritis, RA-like autoimmunity.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: No widely approved CXCL13 antibody; clinical status unclear.
Antibody MoA: Neutralize CXCL13 or block CXCL13-CXCR5 axis.
Safety concerns: Lymphoid architecture disruption, infection, redundancy with other chemokines.
Differentiation hypothesis: Biomarker-rich patient selection using serum/tissue CXCL13 and gland/renal ectopic follicles.

Disease relationship: Fibroinflammatory disease; SSc, PSC and eosinophil/monocyte-fibrosis axis.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: CM-101 anti-CCL24 studied in PSC/SSc; SSc phase 2 listed suspended.
Antibody MoA: Neutralizing antibody; pH-dependent recycling attractive for soluble antigen.
Safety concerns: Chemokine redundancy, eosinophil host defense, uncertain causality.
Differentiation hypothesis: Less crowded fibrosis chemokine axis; CCL24-high tissue/serum biomarker can enrich.

Disease relationship: Fibroblast/epithelial remodeling, inflammation, itch; SSc and HS-like inflammatory fibrosis hypothesis.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: No approved OSMR antibody; OSM/OSMR programs limited/unclear.
Antibody MoA: Block OSMR signaling with Fc-silent IgG or masked inflamed-tissue antibody.
Safety concerns: Wound healing/repair impairment, epithelial toxicity, broad stromal expression.
Differentiation hypothesis: Targets tissue remodeling rather than canonical immune suppression; lesion transcriptomics can select.

Disease relationship: Mucosal inflammation and fibrosis; IBD validates pathway; possible celiac/PSC/SSc overlap.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Anti-TL1A antibodies in IBD pipelines; autoimmune outside IBD less validated.
Antibody MoA: Neutralize TL1A-DR3 signaling.
Safety concerns: Host defense, mucosal immune effects, fibrosis benefit not guaranteed.
Differentiation hypothesis: Extend validated mucosal-fibrotic biology to PSC/celiac immune-active subgroups.

Disease relationship: Skin/neutrophilic inflammation; GPP validated; possible HS and blistering inflammatory subgroups.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Spesolimab approved for GPP; imsidolimab trials in GPP/skin diseases.
Antibody MoA: Block IL-36R signaling.
Safety concerns: Infection/barrier defense, limited non-GPP efficacy.
Differentiation hypothesis: Use IL-36-high lesion biomarker and tissue-localized design; outside GPP competition/failure risk high.

Disease relationship: Refractory celiac disease and tissue-resident cytotoxic lymphocyte activation; possible myositis/alopecia-like biology.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Anti-IL15/IL15R programs historically mixed; no broad approved autoimmune mAb.
Antibody MoA: Neutralize IL-15 or block IL-15 trans-presentation.
Safety concerns: NK/CD8 suppression, infection, malignancy surveillance concerns.
Differentiation hypothesis: Refractory celiac with IL-15/IEL biomarker is a focused niche.

Disease relationship: Controls IL-15 trans-presentation in mucosal and tissue immune activation.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Clinical agents exist historically; current status unclear.
Antibody MoA: Block IL-15 trans-presentation; possible bispecific local design.
Safety concerns: Similar to IL-15 blockade; tissue distribution complexity.
Differentiation hypothesis: May be more selective than pan-IL-15 neutralization if epitope blocks trans-presentation.

Disease relationship: Type I IFN-high SLE, dermatomyositis, Sjögren subsets.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Anifrolumab approved for SLE; renal/myositis/Sjögren use not fully settled.
Antibody MoA: Block type I IFN receptor signaling.
Safety concerns: Viral infection, herpes zoster, vaccination effects.
Differentiation hypothesis: Target validated but crowded; new seed only with tissue-selective, biomarker-specific or combination rationale.

Disease relationship: SSc-ILD, GCA, RA, inflammatory myositis subsets.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Tocilizumab/sarilumab approved in immune diseases; tocilizumab used in SSc-ILD contexts.
Antibody MoA: Block IL-6 signaling.
Safety concerns: Infection, neutropenia, liver enzymes, GI perforation.
Differentiation hypothesis: Validated but crowded; limited novelty unless new format/disease segment.

Disease relationship: Autoantibody diseases with plasma-cell persistence: SLE, refractory pemphigus, IgG4-RD, myositis.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Daratumumab/isatuximab oncology; autoimmune case series/trials limited.
Antibody MoA: Plasma-cell depletion via Fc effector; possible Fc-tuned antibody.
Safety concerns: Infection, hypogammaglobulinemia, cytopenias, infusion reactions.
Differentiation hypothesis: Can address CD20/CD19-resistant plasma-cell disease, but safety may be too oncology-like.

Disease relationship: Plasma-cell and IgA/autoantibody support in SLE/LN, Sjögren, IgA kidney disease.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Atacicept/telitacicept dual BAFF/APRIL; APRIL agents in renal pipelines.
Antibody MoA: Neutralize APRIL, or dual BAFF/APRIL blockade.
Safety concerns: Hypogammaglobulinemia, infection, broad humoral suppression.
Differentiation hypothesis: APRIL-selective design may spare BAFF biology while targeting plasma-cell niches.

Disease relationship: SLE/LN and Sjögren B-cell survival.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Belimumab approved SLE/LN; telitacicept/blisibimod class examples.
Antibody MoA: Neutralize BAFF.
Safety concerns: Infection, mood warnings in label context, slow onset.
Differentiation hypothesis: Useful benchmark but weak novelty unless paired with biomarker or dual design.

Location class: Membrane receptor on B cells/plasma cells
Disease relationship: BAFF/APRIL receptor; altered B-cell differentiation and antibody production.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Atacicept is TACI-Fc ligand trap; receptor-targeting mAbs less established.
Antibody MoA: Block or modulate BAFF/APRIL receptor signaling.
Safety concerns: Immunodeficiency risk; receptor biology complex, genetic CVID association.
Differentiation hypothesis: Direct receptor modulation could differ from ligand traps but biology risk high.

Disease relationship: Long-lived plasma-cell survival; pathogenic autoantibody persistence.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: BCMA CAR-T/TCE/ADC oncology; autoimmune cell therapy interest, antibody-only less clear.
Antibody MoA: Deplete plasma cells; ADC/TCE concept generally high risk in autoimmunity.
Safety concerns: Profound hypogammaglobulinemia, CRS/ICANS for TCE, oncology-like toxicity.
Differentiation hypothesis: Powerful reset concept, but conventional antibody seed should be cautious.

Disease relationship: AAV, myasthenia, dermatomyositis/complement injury, blistering disease.
Existing drugs / clinical agents: Eculizumab/ravulizumab approved in complement-mediated diseases; zilucoplan peptide in gMG.
Antibody MoA: Block C5 cleavage or C5a generation.
Safety concerns: Meningococcal/encapsulated infection, vaccination burden, cost.
Differentiation hypothesis: Validated but crowded; disease entry must justify antibody over existing complement agents.
